comments.body:
A tx that used all its send attempts, but never came back from the network, can no longer be sent again. Now `Add()` can only restarts a tx that is resolved. But `GetStale()` skips such a tx, so nothing marks it resolved.

Are we getting rid of the 'retry' feature..?

If another peer sends us the same tx later, this line replaces the saved peer and time. So `received_by_us` may not show the first peer that sent it back.

Should we keep the first one?
No, that was not intentional. Fixed. Please double check again, this has become non-trivial.
Right, changed it to only set `received_by_us` if it is not set.

comments.body:
> [0aa8193](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36477/changes/0aa81936cf2d51f55eeaca26fd036ad8d5fdc09f) _private broadcast: show finished transactions in getprivatebroadcastinfo_:

Minor inaccuracy: echoed transaction may still have `attempts_remaining > 0` initially. Maybe the text should list the stored categories: transactions being actively sent, sent but not echoed back, and echoed back.

> [0aa8193](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36477/changes/0aa81936cf2d51f55eeaca26fd036ad8d5fdc09f) _private broadcast: show finished transactions in getprivatebroadcastinfo_:

This should also be updated.

Related, what happens when a previously-finished transaction is requested to be private-broadcast again?

- `Add()` sees it finished, and clears `received_by_us` and `resolved`
- It is sent out again (to 3 peers)
- It never gets re-added to our mempool, as it already there. `MarkResolved` is not called again.
- The transaction may be taken as failed
- Final state reported in RPC: `attempts_remaining` 0 and no `received_by_us`

Is this intended this way?

> It never gets re-added to our mempool, as it already there. `MarkResolved` is not called again.

Note that `MarkResolved()` is called after we receive the transaction but before we try to put it in the mempool:

https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/df0dc1e2d2059213e49a9f115fd55a9f0119d26c/src/net_processing.cpp#L4734

https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/df0dc1e2d2059213e49a9f115fd55a9f0119d26c/src/net_processing.cpp#L4770

So, it will be marked as resolved if we receive it, even if it wouldn't enter the mempool because it is already there.

But... would we receive it (a second time)? After the initial receive we would send it to all peers. So all of them know we have it. They wouldn't `INV` it to us anymore and even if they do we wouldn't request it (with `GETDATA`) because we have it in our mempool already.

So, yes, there is no reliable way to know if the second broadcast succeeded. This is the same in `master` right now. There may be new peers in the meantime that are unaware that we have the transaction and they will `INV` it to us (if it even starts propagating a second time through the network). Something to consider, separately from this PR. I do not think this PR changes the behavior.

comments.body: Right. This text is to explain that some transactions will remain (because all others would be removed). Now I think it is not necessary because all will remain, so no need to explain that _some_ particular ones will remain. Dropped the sentence.

Shortened to just:

```
"abortprivatebroadcast",
"Abort private broadcast of a transaction and remove it from the queue.\n"
"This method is only available when running with -privatebroadcast enabled.\n",
```
good?

True, upon a re-request there new new relay will happen. Other nodes and this node will have the TX already in their mempool. As a result, "received_by_us" will never be set, and it will be not possible to decide/observe the success of the second broadcast.

My point was, that if the TX is already in our mempool, and for some strange reason it is relayed back to us after the re-request, our node will not request GETDATA (because TX is in the mempool), the handler will not be called, and the "receive" flags will remain empty.

The behavior on `master` is the same, except that the "received_by_us" flag is a new addition.

I can see these cases:

1. Already in the mempool, and no re-relay happens (the likely case): The "received_by_us" stays empty
2. Already in the mempool, but re-relay happens: The "received_by_us" stays empty -- `AlreadyHaveTx` is true, so no GETDATA is sent, no TX arrives, and the TX handler (`MarkResolved`) is never called.
3. Not in the mempool and re-relay happens: "received_by_us" is set.

Case 2. could be argued about, but I think it's fine. The root of the issue is that upon re-request there will be no new relay.

One idea that we could consider though: upon a re-request don't clean the "received" flag if the TX is already in the mempool (persist that info that we have received it previously; and do perform the new sendouts).
